issues.description: Field mismatch: Animal.name. The Problem Statement text (Part 1 task) explicitly instructs to use a StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute (problem_statement.md lines 84-86). The UML diagram in the same problem statement shows the Animal attribute as name: String (problem_statement.md lines 26-29). The provided reference solution declares the field as private String name in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java (solution_repository). These three artifacts disagree about the attribute type. This confuses students about what type to declare for Animal.name, what the getter/setter signatures should be (String vs StringBuilder), and how example code/tests that call getName() or setName(...) will type-check.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical type for Animal.name and align all materials. Two practical options: (A) Prefer String (recommended to match the existing solution): update the Problem Statement text to remove the StringBuilder recommendation, and ensure the UML shows name: String. Ensure any example code and tests expect getName() to return String. (B) If StringBuilder is desired for pedagogical reasons: update the UML to name: StringBuilder, update the reference solution and template to declare private StringBuilder name and adjust constructor, getName()/setName() signatures and all usages (including tests and example code) to use StringBuilder. Apply the chosen change consistently across problem_statement.md, the template code, and the solution repository.
